intro: GridKya is being built one role at a time. Each role is finished, tested and shown here before the next one starts.

roles.label: GridKya Administrator (dréCAR)
roles.note: Built and tested – opens and suspends agencies, accounts, subscriptions, system settings and the roles guide

roles.label: Owner
roles.note: Built and tested – levies, statements, tenants, property value, home inspection and Ask GridKya

roles.label: Managing Agent
roles.note: First full version – AI Estate Manager, Estate Health Score, board reports, Levies & Payments, people & approvals; to be refined

roles.label: Estate Agent
roles.note: First full version – listings, leads with Buyer Suitability Score, viewings with gate codes, Instant Estate Report, Heat Map; to be refined

roles.label: Trustee
roles.note: First full version – Decision Centre, Risk Dashboard, Health Score, digital voting and board reports; to be refined

roles.label: Tenant
roles.note: Built and tested – Landlord & Rent (invoices, proof of payment, signed lease, late notices), Move-In Assistant and Ask GridKya

roles.label: Contractor
roles.note: First full version – work orders, clock in/out on site, before/after photo check, scorecard; to be refined

updates.title: All roles built: managing agent, trustee, estate agent and contractor
items: Managing agent – AI Estate Manager: a morning brief of urgent repairs, escalating complaints, late contractors, owners in arrears, payments to allocate and approvals
Estate Health Score: security, maintenance, money and compliance, each out of 100, and one overall score – the same for the agent and the trustees
Board report generator: trustee, financial, maintenance and security reports in one click, ready to print or save as PDF

Managing agent – People & approvals: add owners, tenants, trustees, contractors, estate agents and colleagues with their own sign-in; approve requests to be linked to a unit (nobody links themself any more)
The estate manager on site now works in the managing agent’s team (gate, residents, bookings, pets)

Trustee – Decision Centre: proposals with the cost and saving (find a water leak, hand arrears to attorneys, get quotes before a contract renews, a gate camera); one tap starts a trustee vote, tells the agent and logs the repair
Trustee – Risk Dashboard: legal matters, insurance, security incidents, water and electricity losses, arrears and contracts, highest risk first
Estate agent (sales & rentals): listings, leads with a Buyer Suitability Score, viewings, an Instant Estate Report for buyers and an Estate Heat Map
Owners can ask an accredited estate agent to sell or let their unit and follow views, buyers, viewings and offers
Viewings send the buyer a one-time gate code and tell the owner and the tenant living in the unit

Contractor: clock in and out on site (location checked against the estate), before and after photos checked by GridKya, and a Contractor Scorecard ranked automatically – also seen by the agent and trustees
Server rules for every new link, plus fixes: visitor codes, contractor completion photos, and estate agents can never see residents’ chats or money

updates.title: Tenant role, and owner ↔ tenant rent and lease
items: Owner – My Tenant: rent invoices the owner sends (rent, water & electricity, fees), with Paid / Due / Late on each
Tenant – Landlord & Rent: the same invoices and statement, proof-of-payment upload, the signed lease and the landlord’s details
Tenant uploads proof of payment; the owner checks it and accepts it (or says why not) – the rent account updates for both
Automatic late notices: rent is due on the 1st; if it is not paid by the 10th the tenant is told, and so is the owner
The signed rental contract shows on both the owner’s and the tenant’s profile; owners can also upload a lease signed on paper
New owner tile: Documents – a rental contract template filled in with the owner’s details, and application, inspection, deposit refund, renewal, notice, letter of demand and levy clearance forms
Move-In Assistant for new residents: lease, inspection, access tags, vehicles, meter readings, pets, internet and rules – it ticks itself as things get done
Owners who live in their own unit get everything a resident tenant has (visitor codes, gate pass, emergency button, bookings, meters), and can say “I live here” on My units
Managing agent: bills only the tenants of owners who are not on GridKya, and checks their proof of payment; new leases are signed by both tenant and owner
New estate forms: access application (tags and remotes) and pet application
The same rules are enforced on the server, including a daily late-rent check

updates.title: Owner: tile renamed to “My Tenant”
items: The owner’s “My tenants & rent” tile, tab and link are now simply “My Tenant”

updates.title: Roles made clear, and the GridKya Administrator (dréCAR)
items: New GridKya Administrator role for dréCAR – separate from the managing agent, who is a customer that manages complexes
One clear chain of access: dréCAR opens each managing agency and its first managing agent; the agency adds everyone else
Invite only: a cellphone number that nobody added gets no PIN – nobody can sign themselves up or pick their own role
With a real account you only see your own role (a trustee who owns a unit also gets Owner)
Administrator console: open agencies (free trial or paying), add managing agents, suspend and reactivate, block a person’s sign-in, subscriptions per unit and an activity log
“Who does what” guide on the sign-in screen: every role, what it may do and who gives it access
System settings (server, SMS, AI) are now dréCAR only; agencies keep their own bank details
Privacy: dréCAR cannot see levy accounts or residents unless the agency allows support access for 7 days
The same rules are enforced on the server, so no app change can get around them

updates.title: GridKya server built – ready to run on our own server
items: Real shared data: everyone sees the same accounts instead of demo data on each phone
Sign-in PINs are created and checked by the server
Privacy rules on the server: owners only ever receive their own units’ data; nobody but the managing agent can change levy accounts
Live updates: a change by one person reaches everyone else within seconds, and the app still works offline
Free AI on our own server for Ask GridKya and home-inspection photos, with daily limits
Nightly backups, and data kept in South Africa (Johannesburg) – good for POPIA
Next: install it on the server, then connect the app

updates.title: Owner: every Levies & Payments requirement checked end to end
items: Debit order: the owner downloads the pre-filled form, signs and uploads it; the agent activates it; the owner is told
Debit order collections now get a receipt number and a payment confirmation, like every other payment
If the bank returns a debit order unpaid, the owner is warned straight away
Managing agent can raise any additional charge (legal costs, electricity, admin fee, CSOS levy…) on one unit or all units – it shows on the owner’s statement and the owner is notified
Fines, interest and special levies are labelled on the statement; special levies use their own due date
Statement lines on the same day now stay in the order they happened

updates.title: Owner: Property value, Home inspection and Ask GridKya
items: Property Value Tracker: estimated value of each unit with a range and confidence, value over time, area trends and recent sales in the scheme
Estate benchmarking: “your unit grew 4,4% a year – the estate average is 3,4%”
Home inspection: photos and simple yes/no questions per room; flags cracks, damp, leaks and roof problems, how urgent they are, rough cost, and who must fix it (owner or body corporate)
One tap turns an inspection finding into a repair on the managing agent’s job board
Ask GridKya: instant answers about your levy, reference, the rules, pool hours, refuse days, meetings and contacts
Estate information: hours, contacts, emergency numbers and searchable conduct rules in one place
Market data is sample data and photo AI switches on once a provider is connected – both are labelled in the app

updates.title: Owner role and Levies & Payments
items: New Owner home: levies due across all your units and a “Needs your attention” list
Every unit has its own unique payment reference (e.g. ACA-P012)
Managing agent uploads the bank statement (CSV) – payments with the right reference are allocated automatically
Wrong reference? The owner uploads proof of payment and the agent allocates it by hand
Owners get a confirmation and a receipt for every allocated payment
Professional statements with every levy and charge, ready to print or save as PDF
Debit order form, pre-filled, to print, sign and upload
My units, My tenants & rent (renewals, deposits) and Income & costs for tax
Fixes: correct due and overdue dates, tenants no longer see the owner’s levy account, demo data made consistent
